title: Zürich Hauptbahnhof
visualBrief: The Bahnhofplatz clock pavilion and sandstone arcades frame the historic Zürich station. The barrel-roofed concourse carries iron roof trusses, clerestory arches and the four-sided hall clock. Nine platform shelters step across the westbound rail fan.
nativeAxes: The mapped 127-meter hall roof fixes the signed longitudinal axis toward Bahnhofquai. The mapped western tracks, Bahnhofplatz and the two named station points identify the frontages.

geometrySource: Original deterministic geometry built from photo observations, attributed map alignment and standard terrain samples.
materialMethod: Six shared graphs supply sandstone, limestone, granite, painted metal, standing-seam zinc and tinted glazing. The stone openings, trusses, clocks and rails use original geometry.
limitations: The historic wings, main hall, west shed and centerlines use PMTiles plan geometry. Window, truss, roof and architectural sections are reconstructed from the photos.
Terrain supplies approach elevations. The interior concourse and rail bed heights are reconstructed from standard terrain samples and visible station connections.
The model represents the public ground-level concourses and western train hall. Underground tracks, shops, interiors beyond the public hall and moving trains are outside its scope.
